# Carola — OCV reconfiguration against the 2022-09 … 2023-12 reference, month by month

*generated by `code/carola/fig_carola_ocv_reconfiguration.py`; the metric is the pre-registered one of `code/sds/ocv_reconfigure_spec.md` (behaviour block, log transform, reference MAD), read here as a monthly series. It is not a new test, and it carries none.*

Carola Bruecke, Dresden: one support-sized chip per acquisition (69 x 125 cells, 585 support cells, 30 m guard, 200 m ring) of **Girder A**, 436 acquisitions in both orbit directions (290 ASC, 146 DESC). The record splits into a **reference** of 121 chips (2022-09-03 … 2023-12-27), the **series** of 63 chips on 9 months (2024-01 … 2024-09), and 252 post-collapse chips that are counted and never plotted.

```
z(month) = ( median(log x_month) - median(log x_ref) ) / MAD(log x_ref)
x        = gamma2, P            both on the log scale
R        = rms over the two dimensions (gamma2, P)
ref      = 2022-09-03 .. 2023-12-27   n = 121 chips on 16 months
series   = 2024-01-01 .. 2024-09-09   63 chips on 9 months, 2-8 per month
```

The reference is drawn from the 16 months *before* the series, so the origin of everything below is the bridge's own earlier state and not a baseline chosen after the fact. `0` on both axes is that state; it is not a norm and not a threshold.

## Why this window

The record holds 436 chips from 2022-09-03; the series is the last nine months before the collapse, so the reference can only be built from what precedes 2024-01. Three windows were available, and the choice is stated rather than buried because it moves the answer:

| window | chips | months | ASC / DESC | why it is, or is not, used |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| 2023-01 … 2023-12 | 91 | 12 | 61 / 30 | one calendar year, but the shortest reference and it would discard the 2022 chips for no gain in balance |
| **2022-09 … 2023-12** | **121** | **16** | **81 / 40** | **used** — 16 months, every calendar month of a year represented, and the series held out entirely |
| 2022-09 … 2024-09-09 | 184 | 25 | 124 / 60 | the `fig_sds_ocv_reconfigure_carola` reference: it *contains* the series, so it cannot be the origin the series is measured against |

The third window is not wrong — it is the right choice for the SDS plate, which asks how the pre-collapse block differs from the post-collapse one. Here the question is a month against an earlier state, so the origin has to predate the series. The cost of that decision is stated with it: a 2022-09 … 2023-12 origin knows nothing about the 2024 acquisition conditions except through the seasons it shares with 2023.

## The reference is the origin

| dim | column | transform | n_ref | median (log) | median | MAD (log) | 1 MAD = | pooled MAD (log) | scale used |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| gamma2 | `gamma2_mask` | log | 121 | -6.1047 | 0.002232 | 0.9268 | x2.526 | 0.9219 | `mad` |
| P | `P` | log | 121 | -2.2033 | 0.1104 | 0.2379 | x1.269 | 0.2473 | `mad` |

Both dimensions keep the reference MAD: n_ref = 121 is above the `SCALE_MIN_REF = 10` of the 2026-10-22 amendment, so the pooled MAD of the pre-collapse record (184 chips, pre-collapse record, 2022-09-01 … 2024-09-11 (reference + series)) is **not** substituted. It travels beside the reference as the declared sensitivity — `z_pooled` in the JSON reads the same r from that pooled median and MAD, an affine image of z rather than a second estimate. One MAD of gamma2 is a factor x2.526 on that dimension and x1.269 on P.

The reference is *pooled*, not a run of adjacent images: 121 chips over 16 months, with 0 months empty. That is the population the origin stands for, and the moving-block draw resamples it in date order so a draw keeps neighbouring acquisitions together.

`n` is the number of chips the month's median rests on, `✱` marks a month below `SMALL_N = 6` — here 1 of 9, 2024-09 — and `–` would be a cell the record does not contain, never a zero. The interval is the *reference's* uncertainty: 2000 circular moving-block draws of the 121 reference chips with the reference median **and** scale re-estimated inside each draw, the month's chips held fixed. It answers "how well is the origin known", not "how well is the month known".

## The channel split

The same months, re-standardised by an ASCENDING-only and a DESCENDING-only reference. The month's chips do not change — only the median and MAD of the origin — so any difference is the *reference composition*, entangled with the smaller per-month n of a single channel. It is the plate's declared sensitivity to the one window this figure had to choose:

| channel | n_ref | n_series | ref median (log) | ref MAD (log) | max &#124;Δz&#124; | sign flips | cells beyond ±2 | R max |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| ASC (ascending) | 81 | 43 | -5.7106 / -2.2360 | 0.7785 / 0.2700 | 1.25 | 1 | 0 | 1.57 |
| DESC (descending) | 40 | 20 | -7.0348 / -2.1653 | 0.9311 / 0.1531 | 2.09 | 6 | 2 | 2.17 |

Δz is measured against the pooled-reference z of the same month; the two numbers per column are gamma2 / P. The flips are listed in the JSON under `channels.*.summary.sign_flips`. No month moves by more than 2.09 MAD, and the cells that cross ±2 sit in months of 2-3 chips. The pooled ASC+DESC reference stays the headline; this table exists so a reader can see how much of "no signal" rests on that one choice.

## What the series shows

**No month of the series is a departure from the reference.** The largest |z| anywhere in 2024-01 … 2024-09 is 1.86, and beyond ±2 MAD lie no gamma2 month and no P month. The reference band on R is 0.35–2.54; R peaks at 1.52 in 2024-02 (n = 7) and never reaches its 95th percentile. On this record, a bridge two days before its collapse reads as the bridge of sixteen months earlier.

**The largest single excursion is a low, not a high.** 2024-02 carries the largest R (1.52) with z(gamma2) = -1.86 [-2.42, -1.39] and z(P) = -1.09 [-1.48, -0.85] — both *below* the origin, i.e. less echo consistency and less persistence than 2022-09 … 2023-12, not more. Its two intervals exclude zero because the month's median is far from the origin; that is a statement about where the origin sits, not about the month's typicality, since a single reference chip sits ~2 MAD out by construction.

**The series oscillates on a two-to-three-month scale.** gamma2 swings from -1.86 (2024-02) to +1.16 (2024-08) and P from -1.09 (2024-02) to +0.44 (2024-08). The largest two-month change is +2.41 of gamma2 between 2024-02 and 2024-04 (-1.86 -> +0.54); over nine months that is a stretch, not a trend.

**R stays bounded, and its smallest value is an artefact.** R runs 0.18 … 1.52 against a reference band of 0.35–2.54. 2024-03, 2024-09 falls *below* the band, but it holds 2 chips (2024-09-04, 2024-09-09): two chips can agree with the origin on both dimensions by luck, so a low R there is a small sample, not a stabilised bridge. R is an RMS over two dimensions, so one coordinate can carry it — which is why panel (c), not R alone, is the reading.

**The last month before the collapse is not measurable to better than its n.** 2024-09 holds 2 chips (2024-09-04, 2024-09-09), the last of them two days before the event, and is the only month below `SMALL_N = 6`. Its marker is z(gamma2) = -0.25 [-0.50, -0.01], z(P) = -0.03 [-0.32, +0.19], R = 0.18. The interval is narrow because the *origin* is well known, not because the month is: with two chips, the month's own sampling noise is not bounded by anything this figure computes.

**The channel split is the widest uncertainty in the plate.** ASC (n_ref = 81; 2-6 chips per month) shifts a month by at most 1.25 MAD against the pooled origin, flips 1 sign(s) and puts 0 month-dimension cell(s) beyond ±2; DESC (n_ref = 40; 2-3 chips per month) shifts a month by at most 2.09 MAD against the pooled origin, flips 6 sign(s) and puts 2 month-dimension cell(s) beyond ±2. Every sign flip sits within 1.09 MAD of zero, so no excursion moves, but the *sign* of a month close to the origin does depend on which orbit builds it. The DESC redraw rests on 2-3 chips a month, so part of that spread is the month's own n rather than the origin's composition — this figure cannot separate the two, and does not try. The pooled ASC+DESC reference is the pre-registered one; the split is declared, not preferred.

**One sentence.** Between 2024-01-01 and 2024-09-09 the bridge oscillates inside the state it held from 2022-09-03 to 2023-12-27, and nothing in this figure separates the last month from the first.

## What it does not say

* **The binding limit is sampling, not SNR.** A month rests on 2-8 chips, so 2024-09 alone is `thin` (`n = 2 < SMALL_N = 6`) and its "median" *is* the midpoint of two chips. Every other month is 7 or 8 acquisitions, which is enough for a median and not enough for a spread: the monthly marker is the median of the chips that exist, not of the month, and a month with no acquisition would be a gap, not a value.
* **The interval belongs to the reference.** It says how well a 121-chip origin is known under a resampling of those chips. It is not a confidence interval for a monthly value: the month's own sampling noise is not in it. That is why 2024-09's interval is *narrow* — the origin is well known, the month is not — and why an interval that excludes zero (2024-02) still describes a month inside the spread of the reference chips themselves.
* **The reference is seasonally pooled, not seasonal.** Its 16 months contain every calendar month of 2023 once and 2022's September to December once, so the ±2 band mixes seasonal spread with state spread. A baseline per calendar month would need ~7 chips per month, below `SCALE_MIN_REF = 10`: such a reference has no MAD. The band is therefore *wide for a reason*, and a null inside it is weaker evidence than a null inside a tight band would be.
* **The origin is a choice, and the channel split prices it.** ASC: 81 reference chips, 43 in the series, DESC: 40 reference chips, 20 in the series. Rebuilding the origin from one orbit moves a month by up to 2.09 MAD and puts 2 month-dimension cell(s) beyond ±2 — the difference between "no signal" and "two cells outside the band" is which chips the reference is made of. The pooled ASC+DESC reference is the one declared in advance; the split is a declared sensitivity, not a menu.
* **This `gamma2_mask` is not the `gamma2` of the months figure.** The support-sized chip here is 69 x 125 cells with 585 support cells (30 m guard, 200 m ring), and its median `gamma2_mask` is 0.002232 over the reference. The echo-mask γ² of `fig_carola_ocv_months` is computed on the full 80 x 80 girder chip and runs an order of magnitude higher. Only the *standardised* quantity z is comparable between the two figures; the levels are not, and neither is R.
* **The series stops at the collapse, deliberately.** The 252 acquisitions after 2024-09-11 (2024-09-13 … 2026-08-23) are the same bridge in a different state, and they are counted in the audit and carry no value here. The record does not end at the event; the *series* does.
* **No precursor claim.** The metric is descriptive: it says where the last available month (2024-09) sits, and that month is on the reference. The last chip is 2024-09-09 and the next acquisition is after the event, so nothing between them was measured; a series of 7-8 chips a month cannot time, detect or exclude a precursor, and no test is run that would pretend otherwise.
* **No test, no dose, no partner.** The sds H1/H2 machinery needs at least two states per block and, for a dose, an ordered ladder; here one state is sampled monthly. So there is no p-value, no Holm family and no cosine, ±2 MAD is a descriptive band and not a significance threshold, and these magnitudes are in this reference's own units — they are not comparable to the `fig_sds_ocv_reconfigure_carola` amplitudes, whose reference is the whole pre-collapse record (2022-09 … 2024-09-09).

## Reproduce

```
python3 code/carola/fig_carola_ocv_reconfiguration.py            # data + figure
python3 code/carola/fig_carola_ocv_reconfiguration.py --selftest
python3 code/carola/fig_carola_ocv_reconfiguration.py --verify
bash figures/carola/fig_carola_ocv_reconfiguration_carola.sh
```

The run reads `data/carola/support/carola_ocv_channels.csv` (sha256 `3137d0b31fef80b5…`) and `data/carola/support/carola_ocv_channels_meta.json`, and writes `data/carola/ocv_reconfiguration_carola.json`, `data/carola/ocv_reconfiguration_carola_table.csv`, `figures/carola/fig_carola_ocv_reconfiguration_carola.jpg` and this file. No timestamp enters either output, so a second run is byte-identical. `--selftest` re-derives the plate's invariants from the table; `--verify` recomputes the report and diffs it against the committed JSON (floats to 1e-9) before checking the CSV against the same object.

## The figure

* **(a)** z(gamma2) by month: one dot per chip (light), the month's median (filled), the reference's ±2 MAD band (grey), the 95 % reference-uncertainty bar, the chip count `n` in the strip at the bottom, and the collapse of 2024-09-11 as the red cut. The dashed lines are the same months under the ASCENDING- and DESCENDING-only references (panel c's table is their source).
* **(b)** z(P) on the same axis and the same reference — the two panels are read together, never as two independent verdicts.
* **(c)** the plane: the origin is the reference state, the grey cloud is the 121 reference chips, the path runs 2024-01 -> 2024-09 and is coloured by quarter, the thin arrows are the quarter medians, and the terminal month is ringed.
* **(d)** R = rms(z gamma2, z P) per month against the empirical 5-95 % band of the reference chips' own R.
